claims.text: The initial alloy is an as-cast or solution-treated FCC/B2 eutectic HEA with a fine lamellar microstructure.
The initial alloy has no pre-existing grain-boundary embrittlement.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C nucleates and grows ordered LCOs within the B2 phase.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C can produce the proposed ordering without grain coarsening or gross phase decomposition.
Intermediate aging produces a continuous, percolating network of coherent ordered LCOs inside the B2 phase.
The proposed LCOs may have D03 or L12 superstructures.
The LCO network anchors at FCC/B2 phase boundaries and acts as a non-slip barrier.
Ordered regions associated with the B2 phase can pin or hinder dislocation motion.
The LCOs create a high-energy barrier to dislocation cross-slip and transmission across FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
An interconnected LCO network locks the microstructure and suppresses dislocation storage and work hardening.
Dislocation jamming caused by the LCO network produces the transient brittle regime.
Higher-temperature aging above about 700 °C dissolves the LCOs or causes them to lose coherency.
Dissolution or loss of coherency of the LCOs removes pinning and restores dislocation mobility and plastic deformation.
Ductility varies non-monotonically with aging, following a ductile-brittle-ductile sequence.
At peak intermediate aging, elongation falls to near zero and fracture is brittle.
In the as-cast baseline, B2 is uniformly ordered and lacks distinct LCO precipitates.
The fine lamellar FCC/B2 baseline supports substantial work hardening involving dislocation activity in the soft FCC phase.
The embrittlement regime is bounded by the interval in which the LCO network is continuous and coherent, before significant coarsening or intergranular-phase formation.
Sigma phase can occur at grain boundaries and is a possible alternative intergranular explanation.
The critical LCO volume fraction or connectivity threshold and the exact dissolution-temperature window are unknown and composition-dependent.

contradictions.description: The rule parenthetically equates persistence of brittleness after LCO dissolution with recovery occurring without LCO dissolution. These are distinct falsifying observations, not equivalent descriptions of the same observation.
